title: Words from Spanish
kidRule: Many words about food, weather and the wild West came from Spanish. Spanish says its vowels the same clear way every time, so listen to each beat. The 'ee' sound is often spelled with I, as in BURRITO, and many words end with an O or an A you can hear, as in TORNADO!
hint: This word came from Spanish! Say it slowly, one beat at a time, and listen for the clear vowel in every beat, especially the last one.
reminder: Spanish words are spelled beat by beat with clear vowels. An 'ee' sound in the middle is usually the letter I, and the last sound is often a plain O or A.

check.question: Why does TORNADO end with a plain letter O, and not O-W or O-E?
check.correctAnswer: It came from Spanish, where many words end with a clear O or A!
distractors: Because every weather word ends with the letter O
Because O-W is never allowed at the end of a word

words.def: A fast, spinning tube of wind that reaches from a storm cloud to the ground.
words.sent: We learned how a tornado spins in science class.
words.story: This word came from Spanish. It blends 'tronada', which means thunderstorm, with 'tornar', which means to turn!
words.card: The *tornado* was made of feathers, and it left my pillow *torn* and my room fluffy!

words.def: A deep valley with steep rock walls, often with a river at the bottom.
words.sent: A river runs along the bottom of the canyon.
words.story: In Spanish this word is spelled cañón, with a wavy mark over the N. English has no ñ, so we write N-Y instead!
words.card: *Can* you sing into the *canyon*? It will sing right back!

words.def: A sweet flavor, made from the pod of a flower, that is used in ice cream and cakes.
words.sent: I chose one scoop of vanilla ice cream.
words.story: The Spanish word 'vainilla' means 'little pod'. Vanilla comes from the seed pod of an orchid flower!
words.card: The ice cream *van* sold only *vanilla*, so the penguins bought it all!

words.def: A big, happy party or festival with music and dancing.
words.sent: The whole town danced at the fiesta.
words.story: Fiesta is the Spanish word for party. It is a cousin of the English words feast and festival, which all grew from the same Latin word!
words.card: The b*est* part of the *fiesta* was the dancing llama!

words.def: A soft flat bread rolled around beans, rice, and other tasty fillings.
words.sent: Dad wrapped my burrito in shiny foil.
words.story: In Spanish, burrito means 'little donkey'. Nobody knows for sure how the food got that name!
words.card: The *burrito* was so big that it let out a *bur*p!

words.def: A wild animal that looks like a small wolf and howls at night.
words.sent: We heard a coyote howl far away in the hills.
words.story: Spanish speakers borrowed this word from 'coyotl' in Nahuatl, the language of the Aztecs. A coyote can run about 40 miles an hour!
words.card: The *coy* little *coyote* hid behind a cactus and howled, 'Peekaboo!'

words.def: A huge spinning storm with strong wind and rain that forms over warm ocean water.
words.sent: The weather map showed a hurricane far out at sea.
words.story: Spanish sailors learned this word from the Taino people of the Caribbean. Every hurricane is given its own name from a list!
words.card: The *hurricane* blew my candy *cane* all the way to Grandma's house!

words.def: A tall hat with a very wide brim that keeps the sun off.
words.sent: The singer wore a sombrero with silver trim.
words.story: Sombrero comes from 'sombra', the Spanish word for shade, because the wide brim makes shade for your face!
words.card: *Som*e mice had a picnic in the shade of a giant *sombrero*!

words.def: A lunchroom where you carry your food on a tray to a table.
words.sent: We eat lunch in the school cafeteria.
words.story: In Spanish, a cafetería is a coffee shop. The word comes from café, which means coffee!
words.card: The *cafe* next to the *cafeteria* serves spaghetti to squirrels!

words.def: A green dip made from mashed avocados.
words.sent: We scooped up the guacamole with crunchy chips.
words.story: Spanish borrowed this word from Nahuatl, the language of the Aztecs, where 'ahuacamolli' means avocado sauce!
words.card: A *mole* popped out of the garden and asked for chips and *guacamole*!
